mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.25% over the preceding quarter signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 5.25% and remains there for at least two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5% and remains elevated for at least three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of wage inflation offsetting employment losses.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for two consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo MA by >3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months signals a stagflation risk, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails when energy prices drive CPI independently of core inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based demand collapse, which reduces corporate revenue and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline >1% MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of wage stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% in a month following a prior decline signals a consumer-led recovery, which lifts corporate earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in post-recession regimes.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-mo MA by >2% after a prior monthly decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the rebound is driven solely by inventory restocking rather than final demand.
